title: Gated merge decision log & quick heuristics
content:
Purpose:
- Capture lightweight, reusable heuristics for deciding when a PR should go through the full gated-merge (canary + observability hold) vs quick-merge. This is my personal checklist + notes to revisit after next incident.

When to prefer gated merge (hard gate):
- Any change touching the request routing / fallback logic (router/*.ts, routing policy config).
- Changes that alter batching/cache semantics (kv-cache, batching engine).
- Model selection, quantization toggles, or kernel-level changes that affect runtime ops.
- Anything that changes failure/fallback paths (retry/backoff/region fallback).
- Schema changes for persisted metadata (stateful caches, on-disk indexes).

When quick-merge is OK (soft gate):
- Cosmetic refactors limited to a single file + unit tests (no behavioural surface change).
- Docs, readme, tests-only changes.
- Small performance improvements in isolated helper functions with solid benchmarks attached.

Pre-merge quick checklist (5–7 min):
- Does PR touch more than one subsystem? -> if yes, escalate to gated merge.
- Are there new non-idempotent side effects? (DB writes, metrics heavy increments, S3 ops)
- Is there a migration? If so, is it backwards compatible? Migration plan linked?
- Are unit + integration tests present and green? Any flaky/skipped tests added?
- Are there feature flags or rollouts included? Default should be OFF for risky changes.
- Is observability added: tracing spans, metric counters, error labels? If no, request at least minimal telemetry.

Risk scoring rubric (simple, for quick callouts):
- Scope: 1 (single func) – 3 (multi-service)
- Blast radius: 1 (dev-only) – 3 (customer impacting)
- Reversibility: 1 (easy revert) – 3 (migration heavy)
- Observability: 1 (good) – 3 (missing)
Total >= 7 => prefer gated merge and canary.

Canary plan template (copy before merging):
- Canary percentage: 5% traffic to canary variant for 30m.
- Observability dashboard: latency p50/p95, error rate, token throughput, retry rate.
- Alert thresholds pre-baked: p95 > baseline*1.4 OR error_rate > baseline+0.5% triggers immediate rollback.
- Fallback route set to previous model/config with automatic switch on alarm.

Quick refactor ideas (small experiments to reduce merge pain):
- Split routing policy into pure-decision layer + side-effect layer so unit tests can exercise decision without infra. (benefit: fewer gated merges)
- Introduce a tiny "preflight" harness that can run the canary decision code against a small replay of recent requests locally to validate output divergence. (hack: replay 100 random recent traces)
- Add a one-line convention: any PR altering control flow must annotate a short impact blurb at top of PR description (template enforcement).
- Move critical retry/backoff config into a single small module so changes are obvious and easier to reason about.

Follow-ups / TODOs (tickets to open):
- Open ENG ticket: preflight-replay-harness (prototype a local replay runner) [Owner: Matthew]
- Add PR template check in CI to require impact blurb (small GH Action) [Owner: Priya]
- Small experiment: default canary orchestration to 3% and 30m for minor infra changes (metrics-backed).

Shell snippets / handy commands:
- Run limited integration suite locally: ./scripts/run-integration --focus routing --limit 50
- Re-run flaky test with env: TEST_FLAKY=1 pytest tests/integration/test_routing.py::test_prefix_cache
- Local canary replay (ad-hoc): python tools/replay.py --source sample-trace.json --limit 100 --compare

Open questions / things I keep forgetting:
- How to quantify acceptable semantic drift for models in automatic rollouts? Metric suggestion: embedding cosine drift > 0.12 triggers human review. (placeholder metric)
- Do we want a separate lightweight gate for config toggles vs code changes? The threshold is fuzzy.
- Is the fallback toggle always safe across Dedicated + Private? Need to validate per-deployment network constraints.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short; move stable bits to Confluence once iterated.
- Revisit after first canary using this checklist. Capture false positives (times we gated but didn't need to) to calibrate.

Mini post-mortem template to attach to PR if something goes wrong:
- Time of regression, detection method, initial suspect commit, rollback action taken, customer impact summary, monitoring gaps, follow-ups (owner + ETA).

End of dump.

-- mta
